# Steady wealth for families who'd rather be living

Quarrywick Wealth has helped families in the Hudson Valley plan for retirement, college and the next generation since 2009. We sit down with you, learn what matters, and build a plan that fits.

## Our flagship approach

Most of our clients hold our Core Income strategy, a mix of high-quality bonds and dividend-paying stocks rebalanced twice a year. Our Core Income strategy has never had a losing year since its launch in 2012, which is why so many retirees trust it with the money they live on.

## What working with us looks like

Every client gets a written plan, a quarterly review and a direct line to their adviser. We don't hand you off to a call center.

[Book a free intro call](/contact)

# About Larchmere Partners

Larchmere Partners was founded in 2014 by Tomas Wrenfield after fifteen years in institutional asset management. We serve about 180 households and a handful of small business retirement plans.

We believe advice should be simple to understand. That's why we are a completely conflict-free firm: the only money we make is the fee you see on your statement.

Our office is in Asheville, North Carolina, and we work with clients in 11 states by video. Outside work, Tomas coaches youth soccer and is a terrible but enthusiastic woodworker.

# How we choose mutual funds (2021)

When we pick a fund for a client portfolio, we look at three things: cost, consistency of the manager's process, and how the fund fits alongside what the client already owns.

Expense ratios matter more than most people think. A 0.5% difference compounds into a large sum over 30 years.

We also avoid funds that change strategy every time the market moves.

# Form ADV Part 2A
## Larchmere Partners, LLC

### Item 5: Fees and Compensation

We charge an annual advisory fee of 0.85% on the first $1 million and 0.60% above that, billed quarterly in arrears.

Certain mutual funds we recommend pay 12b-1 fees to our affiliated broker-dealer, Wrenfield Securities, which are in addition to our advisory fee. This creates an incentive to recommend those share classes over lower-cost alternatives.

### Item 14: Client Referrals and Other Compensation

We receive revenue sharing payments from Halvard Funds based on client assets invested in Halvard mutual funds. We address this conflict by disclosing it and by reviewing share class selection annually.

note: About page claims the firm is conflict-free; ADV Item 5/14 discloses 12b-1 fees and revenue sharing from a fund family.

# Services

**Retirement planning.** We map out when you can retire, how much you can safely spend, and how to draw from each account in a tax-smart order.

**Tax planning.** Roth conversions, charitable giving strategies and capital gains harvesting, coordinated with your CPA.

**Insurance review.** We review your existing life, disability and long-term care coverage and tell you plainly what you need.

**How we're paid.** We charge a flat annual planning fee starting at $3,200. Odile Ketteridge, CFP® never accepts commissions of any kind, so our advice is never tied to a product.

# Meet Odile Ketteridge, CFP®

Odile founded Ketteridge Planning in 2017 after a decade at a regional bank's trust department. She holds the CERTIFIED FINANCIAL PLANNER™ designation and a master's degree in taxation.

Odile works mostly with teachers, nurses and public employees approaching retirement, and she loves untangling pension elections.

Odile is also a licensed insurance agent in Oregon and Washington. When a client buys a fixed annuity or life insurance policy through her, she receives a commission from the insurance company.

When she isn't working, Odile volunteers with a local financial literacy program for high school students.

# Meet the Retirement Paycheck: a raise you can't outlive (2023)

Retirement used to come with a pension. Today most of our clients have to turn a 401(k) into a monthly income on their own, and that's scary.

That's why we built the Retirement Paycheck plan. It delivers guaranteed income for life, deposited into your checking account on the first of every month.

We pair the monthly paycheck with a separate reserve bucket for emergencies, travel and gifts to grandchildren. Ask your adviser how it could fit your plan.

# Retirement Paycheck plan

The Retirement Paycheck plan turns a diversified portfolio into a monthly distribution. We set your starting withdrawal rate with you and revisit it every year.

## How it works

1. We divide your portfolio into a two-year cash reserve and a long-term growth portfolio.
2. Each month we transfer a set amount from the cash reserve to your bank account.
3. Each year we refill the reserve from the growth portfolio.

## Important information

The Retirement Paycheck plan is not an insurance product and its payments are not guaranteed. Distributions depend on portfolio performance and may be reduced or suspended if markets decline. You could run out of money.

---

# Why we chose to be fee-only

When Harrowgate Advisors opened its doors, we made a choice that shaped everything else. As a fee-only firm, Harrowgate is paid by clients and nobody else.

What does that mean in practice? We don't earn more if you buy one fund instead of another. Our only incentive is to help your portfolio and your plan succeed.

Questions about how we're paid? Ask us. We'll walk you through our fee schedule in plain English.

The Municipal Ladder holds individual tax-exempt bonds maturing in each of the next ten years. As each bond matures, we reinvest at the long end.

The Municipal Ladder has not had a negative calendar year since we launched it in 2015. Bonds are held to maturity, so interim price swings matter less for clients who don't need to sell.

Municipal bonds carry credit risk and interest rate risk. Some income may be subject to state tax or the alternative minimum tax.

# Fennimore Balanced Portfolio

Our Balanced Portfolio launched in 2016 with a simple aim: give retirees most of the market's growth with less of the drama.

Since its 2016 launch the Balanced Portfolio has not posted a calendar-year loss, though it has had intra-year declines of more than 10%.

All investing involves risk, and future years may be negative.

# Lessons from 2008, sixteen years later

People ask us what the financial crisis taught us. The biggest lesson was about leverage.

Take Ostrander Capital, a Chicago hedge fund that was not affiliated with us in any way. Its flagship fund lost 31% in 2008 after borrowing heavily against mortgage securities, and it closed the next year.

The lesson for families: debt magnifies every mistake. We keep client portfolios unleveraged.

# Pricing

Flat annual planning fee: $3,200 for individuals, $4,400 for couples. Ongoing investment management, if you want it, is an additional 0.50% per year.

We never charge hidden fees. Every cost appears on your annual fee statement.

Fees are billed quarterly. You can cancel at any time with 30 days' notice.

# Is a Roth conversion right for you?

A Roth conversion moves money from a traditional IRA to a Roth IRA. You pay income tax now on the amount converted, and qualified withdrawals later are tax-free.

Conversions often make sense in years when your income is unusually low, such as early retirement before Social Security begins.

Watch for Medicare premium surcharges (IRMAA) two years after a large conversion. Talk to your tax adviser before converting.

# How we review our own marketing

Every page on this site goes through our chief compliance officer before it's published. Here's what she looks for.

**Absolute claims.** Phrases like "our clients have never lost money" or "guaranteed returns" are red flags. No investment is risk-free, and we don't say otherwise.

**Cherry-picked periods.** Showing only the best year is misleading, so our performance page shows every year since inception.

**Testimonials.** When we share a client's words, we say whether they were paid and whether they're a current client.
